thread:
alex: Heads-up — acme POC failing when uploading ~4.2MB JSON context via presigned URL. Customer sees 413 from our gateway.

maria: Which endpoint? uploading to hosted S3 or customer bucket?

alex: Hosted. Flow: client requests presign -> we return PUT URL -> client PUTs blob -> PUT returns 413 from CDN/edge. curl shows: HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large and an nginx HTML body.

sam: @alex can you paste exact Content-Length and Content-Type the client is sending? Are they gzip-ing?

alex: Content-Length: 4,246,789; Content-Type: application/json; no gzip. They tried naive client chunking but our presign flow gives a single URL per object so that didn't help.

kim: This smells like client_max_body_size on our nginx proxy (we bumped it down a while back). @eng-infra-bot can you confirm proxy limits for /v1/uploads/*?

eng-infra-bot: Investigating. Current proxy-prod client_max_body_size=4m for /v1/uploads/* (legacy rule). Starting canary rollout of updated config to 10m on prod-edge-canary. ETA ~7m.

maria: Short-term options to propose to customer: 1) gzip before upload (fast) 2) use S3 multipart upload with presigned parts (more work) 3) server-side assembly: client uploads multiple objects and we stitch them.

sam: Note — multipart presigned flow requires them to do the initiate/complete steps. It's doable but many customers prefer a single PUT. Also multipart avoids nginx limit because smaller parts.

alex: Customer wants minimal changes for demo tomorrow. They asked if we can recommend a client-side split + sequential API calls (e.g., split context into N messages and call /v1/ingest append). Is there a documented pattern? Any gotchas with token accounting?

kim: For demo velocity, easiest is temporary proxy limit bump for that org's traffic (via route rules) and add docs for long-term. But that requires an infra ticket and approval.

maria: We should also add an explicit example for gzip + Content-Encoding header — had a customer previously upload compressed without setting header and ingestion broke because we stored compressed blob and model input expected json. Example to share: 

```
# compress then presign-upload
gzip -c context.json > context.json.gz
curl -X PUT -T context.json.gz "${PRESIGNED_URL}" -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
Make sure server-side ingestion detects and gunzips if Content-Encoding present.

sam: I'll draft a lightweight JS shim that does client chunking + upload parts + call /v1/uploads/assemble (lambda) to stitch. Will post repo link in this thread in ~30m.

alex: Customer already tried gzipping but forgot Content-Encoding — they ended up with a compressed object and model errors. Will share that symptom with them.

kim: infra update — canary change applied to prod-edge-canary, no 5xx observed in next 5m. Rolling to prod edges incrementally; full rollout scheduled in 20m if stable. Will open a temporary allowlist rule for acme-org on demo window if they sign off.

maria: I'll send acme a short note: (1) temporary limit bump option, (2) gzip with Content-Encoding example, (3) multipart/presign guidance + offer our JS shim.

alex: appreciated. If prod rollout completes OK we should share permanent docs and an SDK example. :+1:

sam: posting shim link soon — includes token-size guidance (split by approx 1.8k tokens per chunk) and retry logic for part uploads.

alex: thanks everyone — I'll update the customer and loop back once I have their decision. :pray:
